methodology: Unweighted simple average of the candidate’s share in each opened national 2028 GOP primary poll that reported that candidate (8 polls). These polls use different universes (open-ended intended primary voters; likely Republican primary voters; GOP side of a midterm-voter survey; likely voters; self-selected GOP-primary RVs; Emerson closed-ended list of GOP-primary RVs; Verasight list question among Republican adults) and are not strictly comparable. A RealClearPolitics 2028 nomination page was blocked (403) and was not used. Aggregator tables that were not opened as primary sources were not used, except that the Echelon Insights result was read from a Polling Desk poll page that cites the NYT/PollResults feed. Nov 20, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary polls were found since the Emerson release (Nov 19). Posts on X reported that the RealClearPolitics 2028 average now shows Rubio 35.4% and Vance 34.0%; the RCP page again returned 403, so that figure is not used here. Nov 21, 2026: added the Strength In Numbers/Verasight poll (Nov 11–13; released Nov 19), which had been missed. Average moved from Vance 35.0 / Rubio 31.3 / DeSantis 12.3 (6 polls) to Vance 33.9 / Rubio 31.6 / DeSantis 13.3 (8 polls). A First Tuesday Strategies South Carolina poll (Nov 19, 2,062 RV: Rubio 38.5, Vance 16.8, DeSantis 13.4, as relayed on X) is a single-state poll and is not part of this national average. The RCP 2028 page again returned 403 and was not used. Nov 22, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary polls; the RealClearPolling latest-polls page (opened this time) still lists Emerson (Nov 19) as the newest. Online straw polls relayed on X (StrawPoll.us: Rubio 48.2, Vance 19.7; the “People’s Poll”: Rubio 57, Vance 7) are self-selected and not used. Averages unchanged. Nov 23, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary poll. The Washington Examiner (Byron York, Nov 23) published early-state head-to-head results from the OnMessage Inc. poll for the Combat Antisemitism Movement (Nov 7–10; 1,000 likely GOP voters, 250 each in IA, NH, SC, NV; MoE ±3.1): Iowa Rubio 49 / Vance 28; New Hampshire 44 / 25; South Carolina 43 / 28; Nevada 53 / 32. Poll relays on X give four-state combined figures of Rubio 47 / Vance 28 (multi-candidate) and Rubio 52 / Vance 31 (head-to-head), not confirmed in the column. DeSantis was not included. As a set of single-state samples for an advocacy sponsor, it is not part of this national average. Averages unchanged. Nov 24, 2026: added the Rainey Center poll (Bedrock Polling, Nov 8–12, 406 LV: Vance 36, Rubio 24, DeSantis 10, Trump Jr. 7, Cruz 4, Kennedy 4), read from the Polling Forecast poll page. Average moved from Vance 33.9 / Rubio 31.6 / DeSantis 13.3 (7 polls) to Vance 34.1 / Rubio 30.6 / DeSantis 12.9 (8 polls). No new national 2028 GOP primary poll was released Nov 23–24. CNN’s Harry Enten (Nov 22 segment, widely relayed Nov 23–24) summarized national polling as Rubio 34, Vance 30; that is an analyst’s summary, not a poll, and is not used. A HispanicsVote/Newsweek poll of Florida Hispanic Republicans (Oct 14–18: Rubio 57, DeSantis 25, Vance 10), relayed on X Nov 23, is a single-state subgroup and is not used. Stephen Miller has not been listed in any opened 2028 primary poll. Nov 25, 2026: no new national 2028 GOP primary poll found; averages recomputed and unchanged (Vance 34.1 / Rubio 30.6 / DeSantis 12.9, 8 polls). New state poll, not used in this national average: Riparian Research survey of 1,045 Arizona registered Republicans (SMS text-to-web, Nov 20–24; MoE ±3.0; sponsor not stated), read from the Arizona Insiders article and toplines PDF: Rubio 48.8, Vance 24.9, DeSantis 14.2, Haley 3.1, Youngkin 0.9, Carlson 0.7, none 5.9; second choice Vance 31.8, Rubio 30.1, DeSantis 26.8 (63.1% of Vance voters name Rubio second; 48.0% of Rubio voters name Vance second). Aggregators opened Nov 25 differ: PollCheck (Nov 24) Vance 33.7 / Rubio 32.0; Vote-Scope (Nov 24, weighted) Vance 35.8 / Rubio 24.3; Politix+ (Nov 25, 20 polls) Rubio 36.0 / Vance 30.0. Politix+ lists McLaughlin (Nov 5) and AtlasIntel (Nov 1) polls not opened as primary sources here. Kalshi/PredictIt market prices are not polls. Stephen Miller is not listed in any opened 2028 primary poll.

polls.sample: 418 Republican primary voters within a national survey of 1,000 registered voters
polls.universe: Registered voters planning to vote in the GOP primary (closed-ended list)
polls.moe: ±3 points on the 1,000 voters; subsample MoE not stated.
polls.note: Released Nov 19, 2026. The closed-ended list question (44 / 24 / 9) is used in the average because the other polls here mostly read from candidate lists; the open-ended question had Rubio 36, Vance 20, DeSantis 7, Trump 7, Massie 7. USA Today notes the same pollster had Vance ahead of Rubio 54%–6% a year earlier. Subsample size (418) from USA Today.

polls.moe: About ±4.9 points (per the Polling Desk page).
polls.note: Published Nov 17, 2026. Echelon's previous poll (ended Oct 19) had Vance +18 over Rubio; this one is Vance +14. Read from the Polling Desk poll page (data feed: The New York Times via PollResults.org); the Echelon release itself was not opened.

polls.sample: Republican-primary voters within an online survey of 920 registered voters (39% chose the GOP primary); subsample size not stated.
polls.universe: Self-selected GOP primary voters (all RVs asked which primary)
polls.moe: ±4.2 points on the 920 RVs; larger for the primary sample (not stated).
polls.note: Online via Cint, weighted with an MRP frame. Without Vance: Rubio 42, DeSantis 18, Cruz 8, Carlson 7. Same poll: Ossoff and Newsom each lead Vance by 13 in general-election matchups. A newer, small pollster whose questions were crowdsourced from X followers; treat with caution.

polls.sample: 632 Republicans (listed as 632 A by PollResults) within a national survey of about 1,400 adults from both parties
polls.moe: ±2.6 points on the full survey (Political Wire); about ±3.9 on the 632-person GOP sample (Polling Desk).
polls.note: Released Nov 19, 2026 (missed in the Nov 20 update). The poll asked an open text-box question and then a candidate-list question. The 33 / 27 / 19 figures (Don't know 8, None 5) are reported by Political Wire, PollResults and the New York Daily News and are used in the average, consistent with using closed-ended list questions elsewhere. Polling Desk (NYT/PollResults feed) lists 26 / 19 / 9 for the same field dates and sample; which question that reflects was not confirmed on a page opened, so it is shown separately and not averaged. G. Elliott Morris: 'Rubio’s lead comes almost entirely from the hawks'; Vance leads among Republicans who want to end the Iran war and among white blue-collar workers. Verasight’s previous reading (ended Apr 23) had Vance +21, per Polling Desk.

polls.sample: Intended 2028 Republican primary voters, within a survey of 1,685 U.S. adult citizens. GOP subsample size was not stated on the article page.
polls.moe: Parent poll ~±3 percentage points (1,685 adults); subsample MoE not stated.
polls.note: Open-ended question, AI-coded. Also reports MAGA split: Vance 45 / Rubio 35 / DeSantis 10; non-MAGA: Vance 33 / Rubio 29 / DeSantis 19.

polls.sample: Likely Republican primary voters, from a survey of 1,090 U.S. likely voters conducted Nov 5 and 8–9, 2026. GOP subsample size was not stated on the public (non-paywalled) page.
polls.moe: ±3 percentage points on the 1,090 likely-voter survey; subsample MoE not stated on the public page.
polls.note: Public write-up compares to July: Vance down from 39%; Rubio unchanged; DeSantis up from 7%. Other candidates were not listed on the public portion of the page. Field work by Pulse Opinion Research, LLC.

polls.sample: 3,000 midterm voters (National Voter Trends post-mortem). GOP 2028 subsample size was not stated.
polls.note: Cygnal says “on the GOP side” Rubio leads Vance 34–31, with DeSantis third at 14%. Traditional Republicans prefer Rubio 36% to Vance 30%. Other candidates were not listed in this write-up.

other_candidates_note: Mean share among only the opened polls that reported each candidate (n_polls shown); not comparable to the three-candidate average, which every poll reports. Donald Trump (constitutionally barred) is excluded. Stephen Miller has not been listed in any opened 2028 primary poll.
